title: Design Task Manager
statement:
Build a class `TaskManager` that holds a pool of tasks. Each task has an id, an owner `userId` and a priority, and one user may own any number of tasks.

- `TaskManager(tasks)` fills the pool from `tasks`, where each entry `[userId, taskId, priority]` describes one task. The ids in `tasks` are all different.
- `add(userId, taskId, priority)` puts a new task into the pool. No task currently in the pool has the id `taskId`.
- `edit(taskId, newPriority)` sets the priority of task `taskId`, which is in the pool, to `newPriority`.
- `rmv(taskId)` takes task `taskId`, which is in the pool, out of it.
- `execTop()` runs the task with the largest priority (on a tie, the one with the largest `taskId`), takes it out of the pool, and returns its owner's `userId`. When the pool is empty it returns `-1`.

An id that has left the pool, by `rmv` or `execTop`, may be added again later, possibly for a different user.
constraints: The task ids in tasks are distinct
add is only called with an id that is not in the pool; edit and rmv only with an id that is
At most 2 * 10^5 calls in total are made to add, edit, rmv and execTop

signature.name: TaskManager
methods: void add(int userId, int taskId, int priority)

notes:
## Intuition

Scanning every task on each `execTop` costs O(n) per call. A max-heap of `[priority, taskId]` entries keeps the next task to run on top, but a heap cannot cheaply find and change an arbitrary entry, as `edit` and `rmv` would need. So they leave the heap alone: a map `tasks` holds the true owner and priority of every task in the pool, `edit` pushes a fresh entry, and `rmv` only deletes from the map. An entry that disagrees with the map is *stale*, and `execTop` discards stale entries as they reach the top.

## Approach

1. `tasks` maps each task id in the pool to its `{ userId, priority }` record; `heap` holds `[priority, taskId]` entries. The constructor calls `add` for each starting task.
2. `add` records the task and pushes `[priority, taskId]`.
3. `edit` changes the record's priority and pushes `[newPriority, taskId]`.
4. `rmv` deletes the task from `tasks` only.
5. `execTop` pops entries until one names a task still in `tasks` with exactly that priority, deletes that task and returns its `userId`. If the heap runs out first, it returns `-1`.
6. `before(a, b)` orders the heap: higher priority first, then higher task id. `push` sifts a new entry up; `pop` moves the last entry to the root and sifts it down.

## Example 1, step by step

The constructor pushes `[10, 101]`, `[20, 102]` and `[15, 103]`, and `add(4, 104, 5)` pushes `[5, 104]`. `edit(102, 8)` pushes `[8, 102]`. The first `execTop` pops `[20, 102]`, stale because task 102 now has priority 8, then `[15, 103]`, which is live: task 103 leaves the pool and user `3` is returned. `rmv(101)` makes `[10, 101]` stale. `add(5, 105, 15)` pushes `[15, 105]`, the new top, so the last `execTop` returns user `5`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) to build, O(log m) per `add` and `edit`, O(1) per `rmv`, and amortized O(log m) per `execTop`, where m counts every entry ever pushed: each is popped at most once.
- Space: O(m), one entry per added task and per edit.

## Pitfalls

- On equal priorities the larger task id runs first, not the task added first.
- Checking only that the task exists is not enough: after an edit, the old entry names a task in the pool with an outdated priority.
- Read the owner from the map, not from a heap entry: a removed id can come back with a different user.
- Stale entries can remain when the pool is empty, so pop until the heap is empty before returning `-1`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tasks` | map from each task id in the pool to its `{ userId, priority }` record |
| `heap` | max-heap of `[priority, taskId]` entries, some stale |
| `task` | the record a popped entry names, or `undefined` if that task left the pool |
| `before` | true when entry `a` belongs above entry `b` |
| `top`, `last` | the root being popped and the last entry moved into its place |
| `index`, `parent`, `left`, `right`, `best` | positions used while sifting |
